newsitem.title: INDIA: India industry to rebound, Finance official says.
newsitem.headline: India industry to rebound, Finance official says.

text.p: A slowdown in Indian industrial growth may soon be reversed and a growth recovery in the second half of 1997/98 (April-March) is imminent, Finance Secretary Montek Singh Ahluwalia said.
Ahluwalia said in a statement in Paris which was released in the Indian capital on Wednesday that the slowdown in industrial growth in the later months of 1996/97 was a matter of concern.
He said the slowdown was attributable to a number of factors including constraints on infrastructure, credit market conditions, lower demand for exports and some slackening in investment activity.
"I am happy to say that there are signs that the industrial slowdown may soon be reversed," Ahluwalia said.
He noted a revival of non-petroleum exports, a pickup in credit growth, low inventories in several industries, a pickup in investment by foreign institutional investors and a rising stock market.

"We believe the 'feel good' index is up again, the animal spirits of the Indian and international investor vis-a-vis India have revived and a growth recovery is imminent in the second half of the current financial year," Ahluwalia said.
The finance secretary, the highest ranking civil servant in the ministry, said the government saw the prospect of sustained growth in per capita income of six percent or more per year in the future.
Ahluwalia was addressing India Development Forum meeting in Paris which ended on Wednesday.
